channel.title: Blindspot
channel.description: Independent, rigorous analysis of geopolitics, global economy, security, technology, and power. What mainstream coverage leaves out.

item.title: Former Denver Broncos Star and Veteran ESPN Analyst Tom Jackson Dies at 75
item.description: Former NFL linebacker and broadcast icon Tom Jackson has passed away at 75. His career tracked the rise of modern sports media ecosystems.

item.title: NATO pledges to defend Poland after a Russian missile incursion
item.description: The western alliance has reaffirmed its mutual defense guarantees following a Russian missile breach, exposing the quiet vulnerabilities of eastern border surveillance.

item.title: US intelligence chief says calling Putin a friend is entirely appropriate
item.description: Recent statements from US intelligence leadership endorsing Donald Trump's rhetoric point to a deeper shift in how major powers manage high-stakes diplomacy. Markets and traditional security analysts are forced to reevaluate the mechanics of trilateral engagement.

item.title: The Systemic Infrastructure Debt Behind America's Cascading Technical Outages
item.description: Cascading operational failures across aviation, banking, and federal networks revealed deep structural fragility across Western critical systems. Public panic blamed AI-driven cyber warfare, but the underlying vulnerability remains neglected physical infrastructure.

item.title: COP31 Climate Summit Collapses as Nations Reject Compromise on Fossil Fuels
item.description: Multilateral negotiations in chaos after delegates refuse to sign a final draft omitting explicit decarbonization language. The failure signals a pivot toward unilateral economic policy over consensus diplomacy.

item.title: Baltic Towing Operation Exposes Expansion of Ukrainian Long Range Maritime Strike Capability
item.description: Finnish authorities confirmed Russia is towing a drone-damaged cargo ship in Baltic waters. The incident marks a strategic shift as naval gray-zone targeting moves beyond the Black Sea.

item.title: Fatal Niger Delta Boat Capsizing Highlights Systemic Waterway Safety Failure
item.description: At least 24 mourners drowned when an overcrowded vessel sank in Bayelsa State. The tragedy exposes persistent regulatory gaps and transport infrastructure neglect across rural Nigeria.

item.title: Mexican cartel boss capture sparks deadly Guasave firefight and tests security strategy
item.description: The arrest of Fausto Isidro Meza Flores in Sinaloa left 11 dead after intense urban combat. Beneath the diplomatic celebrations lies the recurring risk of violent fragmentation.

item.title: Paolo Bulgari Dies at 89 as Era of Independent Luxury Dynasties Ends
item.description: The former chairman of the Italian jewelry giant has died in Rome at age 89. His tenure expanded a historic family business into a global empire, setting the stage for corporate consolidation in European luxury.

item.title: Russian Barrage Targets Western Ukraine Logistics Hubs and Critical Energy Infrastructure
item.description: Moscow launched a multi-axis air strike utilizing hundreds of drones and missiles aimed at western Ukrainian rail and power infrastructure. The strikes mark an escalating effort to degrade border logistics connecting Kyiv to European supply lines.

item.title: Federal Indictment Uncovers Systemic Freight Rail Vulnerabilities in California Cargo Heists
item.description: Federal charges against a 14-person theft syndicate in California reveal how simple physical interventions can paralyze heavy rail networks and breach corporate supply chains. The $22 million operation highlights persistent security exposures along major trade arteries.

item.title: Microsoft Incident Report Exposes Structural Risks in Enterprise Cloud Infrastructure
item.description: Microsoft’s final post-mortem on a recent global Outlook outage reveals how internal testing failures and backfiring safety mechanisms paralyzed communications. The episode highlights how extreme cloud consolidation turns routine software updates into critical threats to global infrastructure.

item.title: White House orders federal contractors to clear congressional inquiries
item.description: A new directive requires federal contractors to vet responses to Congress through the White House, reshaping oversight dynamics. The move centralizes executive control over information from private entities executing public funds.

item.title: Bitcoin Rebounds After Hitting Two Year Low Amid Violent Liquidity Sweep
item.description: Cryptocurrency markets endured sharp volatility after Bitcoin touched a multi-year trough before staging a rapid bounce. The violent price action highlights structural fragility and systemic leverage clearing across global derivative desks.

item.title: Washington Denies Iranian Claims That Missile Damaged US F-16 Fighter Over Persian Gulf
item.description: Tehran claimed its air defense systems struck an American fighter jet in international airspace, an account swiftly refuted by United States defense officials. The friction highlights high-stakes narrative posturing across strategic maritime channels.

item.title: Fatal power station fire exposes the systemic decay of Iraq's energy grid
item.description: A deadly blaze at the Hartha power station halted 800 megawatts of generation capacity, laying bare the deep vulnerabilities of Iraq's neglected electrical infrastructure.

item.title: Netanyahu Revives High-Stakes Sectarian Rhetoric as Domestic Coalition Pressures Mount
item.description: Benjamin Netanyahu faces sharp backlash for targeting 19 Arab members of the Knesset in a political survival bid. The escalating rhetoric exposes structural fractures as regional security pressures intensify.

item.title: Deep Andean Quake Avoids Immediate Disaster but Highlights Infrastructure Risks
item.description: A powerful 6.9 magnitude earthquake struck central Peru without causing immediate casualties. Beneath the relief lies a recurring threat to the high-altitude infrastructure connecting the interior to coastal ports.

item.title: Seismic failure: the infrastructure gaps exposed by Peru's latest earthquake
item.description: A 6.9 magnitude earthquake on November 20 crippled power grids and blocked key roads, revealing the precarious state of Andean infrastructure. The event highlights a systemic inability to maintain continuity during crises.

item.title: Trump and Xi Agree Humans Must Retain Control Over Military AI Decisions
item.description: U.S. and Chinese leaders established a consensus on keeping human oversight over military artificial intelligence. However, the lack of verification mechanisms exposes the rift between diplomatic optics and battlefield capabilities.

item.title: Salvadoran Casualties in Haiti Expose Strategic Limits of Exported Anti-Gang Models
item.description: Two Salvadoran soldiers were killed handling explosives in Port-au-Prince during security operations. The tragic incident underscores the severe operational frictions of deploying foreign containment strategies into fractured host nations.

item.title: Tech Stocks Drop as S&P 500 Falls 3.7 Percent and Nasdaq Erases Gains
item.description: A severe equity sell-off pushed the S&P 500 down 3.7% and forced the Nasdaq composite into negative territory for the year. The market drop highlights growing institutional resistance to capital-intensive technology spending under high interest rates.

item.title: Industrial blaze at major US foie gras facility highlights mounting regulatory and operational pressure
item.description: A multi-department emergency response destroyed key production infrastructure at Hudson Valley Foie Gras. The operational disruption coincides with a wave of municipal bans reshaping the market.

item.title: Trump Threatens Tax Penalties on U.S. Tech Firms Building AI Data Centers Overseas
item.description: The U.S. administration proposes strict tariffs and construction bans on foreign data infrastructure to restrict Chinese access to computing power. The move threatens U.S. hyperscalers already facing domestic grid bottlenecks.

item.title: Kyiv Embassies Damaged in Day-Long Russian Barrage as Ukraine Hits Kerch Bridge
item.description: A devastating aerial assault on Kyiv has damaged European diplomatic missions and key urban infrastructure. At the same time, Ukrainian forces successfully disrupted Russia's primary rail link to Crimea.

item.title: Moscow Targets Kyiv Dnieper Bridges in Retaliation for Kerch Strait Attacks
item.description: A overnight barrage of Russian drones and missiles struck three key transit bridges in Kyiv, killing three municipal workers. The strikes on capital river crossings follow consecutive Ukrainian attacks against Crimea's Kerch Strait Bridge.

item.title: The death of Fiona the hippo exposes vulnerabilities in zoo exhibit security
item.description: Fiona the Cincinnati Zoo hippo has died at age nine after swallowing a visitor's hat, exposing systemic gaps in enclosure security.

item.title: Haitian Security Forces Retake Vital Corridor in Major Anti-Gang Offensive
item.description: A joint push by police and private security contractors killed 34 suspected gang members in Martissant. Long-term stabilization remains uncertain without institutional holding power.

item.title: Trump's Pick for Federal Election Security Agency Claims January 6 Was Not an Attack
item.description: The nomination of a January 6 skeptic to head the nation's election security agency signals a structural shift in federal oversight. This move threatens to politicize core institutional guardrails protecting American electoral infrastructure.

item.title: Nvidia targets Arm chief Rene Haas as board rejects Jensen Huang return
item.description: Nvidia's search for a successor to Jensen Huang has led recruiters to Arm chief executive Rene Haas. While markets fixate on political lobbying and executive drama, the move threatens the neutral architecture underpinning global chip design.
